samples.summary: Band painter assigns a persisted, unvalidated colour string straight to `ctx.fillStyle`; an invalid non-empty value silently leaves the previous fill in force, letting document content paint an opaque band in a stale colour over text
samples.evidence: `drawInlineRunBackgroundsForLine` filters only falsy results (`resolveColor(style.backgroundColor) || undefined`, line 263-265) and then does `ctx.fillStyle = color` with no `save()/restore()` and no normalisation through `resolveStoredColor`/`toRgbHexColor`. `style.backgroundColor` is a *persisted* `StoredColor` that, per packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:59-65, arrives from the content PUT API, DOCX/PPTX import and hand-edited CRDT state — the static type is a claim, not a guarantee. A collaborator/importer supplying e.g. `"not-a-color"` makes the canvas ignore the assignment (the exact failure mode documented for issue #728 at color.ts:41-45), so the band is filled with whatever fillStyle the previous pass left (text colour, selection fill), and coalescing now makes that band span a whole line rather than one word — i.e. attacker-authored content can obscure a line of text in another viewer's render. Vector traced to the fillStyle assignment; I could not confirm any confidentiality/authz impact, so this is UI-integrity only and the same unvalidated assignment pre-existed in the per-run loops this replaces.
